correctness.rationale: The first-order average was independently reconstructed from the printed ODE and the source's own inverse linear change rather than from the source's averaged formulas. With \(X=r\cos\theta\), \(Y=r\sin\theta\), symbolic angular integration gives \(\bar f_r=r(eU-j_1-a_1\omega^2)/(2\omega^3)\), \(\bar f_Z=Z(j_1-eU-d_1\omega^2)/\omega^3\), and \(\bar f_U=(-2c_1U+2Z^2/\omega^4+r^2/(1+\omega^2))/(2\omega)\). These disagree in sign with the two printed source averages. A simple positive-radius zero therefore has \(U_*=(a_1\omega^2+j_1)/e\), \(Z_*=0\), and \(r_*^2=2c_1(1+\omega^2)(a_1\omega^2+j_1)/e\), with nondegeneracy requiring \(a_1+d_1\ne0\). The averaged Jacobian splits into one eigenvalue \(-(a_1+d_1)/\omega\) and a quadratic whose Hurwitz conditions are exactly \(c_1>0\) and \(a_1\omega^2+j_1<0\). The stated stable and sign-reversal witnesses follow.
residual_risks: First-order averaging certifies only the small-periodic-orbit branch associated with a simple positive-radius averaged zero.
